answer: Each bonded identity posts collateral in escrow, so splitting stake across aliases does not dilute exposure: when k identities equivocate in coordination, pairwise attribution creates O(k²) penalized relationships. Detection can trigger asymmetric depreciation and compounding forfeitures, making a sybil swarm’s capital loss rise by an exponential multiplier rather than a simple per-account fine. A juniper-like cluster cannot hide shared proofs in a nectar of aliases or find an oasis from slashable evidence.
